acceptance: WebSocket/SSE/WebRTC capability manifests express transport availability, backpressure and fallback requirements.

positive.fixture: a real WebSocket resumes after the last sequence with no repeats or holes, SSE resumes from Last-Event-ID, a WebRTC data channel carries a message, negotiation picks native or fallback transports and records why others were skipped

negative.fixture: an unacknowledged input becomes unknown and is resent only if declared repeatable, a source that cannot resume reports a gap, reconnect attempts are finite with bounded backoff, input queued while down is discarded, a manifest that hides why a transport is missing is refused, no usable transport keeps the source interface
negative.command: pnpm --filter @vsf/specialized-tests exec playwright test specs/transport.spec.ts -g unknown|finite|cannot resume|discarded|hides why|offers no transport

versions.schema: vsf-transport-capabilities-v1 manifest in package; no wire contract yet

security_and_source_permissions: Manifests record what the source offers, never what the browser has; permission-gated transports need the grant by name; unbounded buffering is refused; unknown writes are never resent.
performance_memory_storage: Pipe and OutboundQueue are bounded; sustained pressure stays within the declared byte limit in the unit test.
known_limitations: The reconnect client is test code, not a shipped client
WebRTC was exercised with a loopback data channel only; signalling, real peers and permissions are not covered
HTTP polling is declared and negotiated but has no client
Only Chromium 141 on Linux was run
